title: Rome vs Barcelona: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Rome for ancient history, iconic pasta, and the Eternal City magic. Barcelona for beaches, Gaudí, nightlife, and cosmopolitan livability. Both deserve a visit.

categories.name: Ancient History
categories.summary: Rome wins decisively — 2,500 years of Western civilization in one walkable city.

categories.name: Modern Architecture
categories.summary: Gaudí's Sagrada Família, Casa Batlló, and Park Güell are architectural masterpieces unlike anything in Rome.

categories.name: Food
categories.summary: Rome wins for iconic pasta perfection; Barcelona wins for consistent quality and tapas variety.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Barcelona has 4.5km of urban beaches on the metro. Rome has no urban beach.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Barcelona is one of Europe's club capitals. Rome has excellent aperitivo culture but winds down earlier.

categories.name: Public Transit
categories.summary: Barcelona's metro is more extensive and cheaper. Rome's historic center is walkable.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Rome's access to Naples, Pompeii, Amalfi, and Florence is unmatched.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Both mid-range; Rome has more free iconic sights and cheaper street food.

categories.name: Safety
categories.summary: Both have pickpockets in tourist areas. Barcelona rated safer overall, especially for solo women.

categories.name: Summer Weather
categories.summary: Barcelona's sea breeze keeps summers manageable. Rome's July-August is brutal at 35-38°C.

faq.question: Is Rome or Barcelona better for first-time visitors to Europe?
faq.answer: Rome has a special magic for history lovers; Barcelona wins for cosmopolitan beach-city vibes.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Rome or Barcelona?
faq.answer: Both cost €65-110/day mid-range. Rome edges slightly cheaper due to more free sights and cheaper street food.

faq.question: Which has better food, Rome or Barcelona?
faq.answer: Tie. Rome wins for iconic pasta perfection; Barcelona wins for consistency and tapas variety.

faq.question: Does Rome or Barcelona have better beaches?
faq.answer: Barcelona — 4.5km of urban beaches on the metro. Rome has no urban beach.

faq.question: How many days do you need?
faq.answer: Rome: 4-5 days minimum. Barcelona: 3-4 days for the essentials.

faq.question: Can you visit both?
faq.answer: Yes — 2-hour flight, €40-150 return. 10-12 days splits perfectly between the two cities.
